p.i: Non enim moles Pariæ columnæ, Phidiæ aut vivax ebur, aut Myronis Æra, mansuræ poterunt sacrare Nomina famæ.
Obruet longos cita mors labores, Obruet claros titulos, opésque, Saxa findentur vitiata serae Dente senectæ.
Mulciber quamuis & iniqua Juno Verterint urbem Priami superbam, Illa Smyrnæis inimica pensat Fata Camœnis.
Nec suo mallet cineri superstes Ilium Eois dare jura terris, Quà patent fuscos Rhodope ab nivosa Usque sub Indos.
Sola doctorum monumenta vatum Nesciunt fati imperium severi, Sola contemnunt Phlegetonta, & Orci Jura severa.
SAluete festis deliciis sacræ Maia calendæ, lætitiæ & mero Ludisque dicatæ jocisque, Et teneris Charitum choreis.

page.notes: No margin notes. Right margin shows faint show-through from the reverse page, not transcribed. The initial S of "Saluete" is a large decorative initial and is joined to its word. The first stanza's opening is a continuation from the previous page only in layout; the verse itself starts here, so cont="true" is applied to the first stanza as a fragment of the preceding poem.
